value: The soleus H-reflex, and whether operantly down-conditioning it improves locomotion in people with chronic incomplete spinal cord injury.
Can people with chronic incomplete spinal cord injury down-condition the soleus H-reflex operantly, and if so is the reflex decrease accompanied by improved locomotion?

In 13 people with chronic incomplete spinal cord injury, 30 sessions of operant down-conditioning reduced the soleus H-reflex in two-thirds of the conditioned group, and those subjects walked faster and more symmetrically with better bilateral EMG modulation, establishing spinal reflex conditioning as a targeted rehabilitation method.

quote: After a baseline period in which soleus H-reflex size was measured and locomotion was assessed, subjects completed either 30 H-reflex down-conditioning sessions (DC subjects) or 30 sessions in which the H-reflex was simply measured [unconditioned (UC) subjects], and locomotion was reassessed.
They suggest that operant conditioning protocols could provide a valuable new approach to restoring useful function after spinal cord injuries or in other neuromuscular disorders.

quote: To explore the therapeutic application of these protocols, we studied the impact of down-conditioning the soleus H-reflex in people with impaired locomotion caused by chronic incomplete spinal cord injury.
